Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.
I’ll first read the workspace instructions, then inspect the inherited rollout evidence and both required control skills before touching the policy. I’ll keep all edits inside this Phase 2 workspace.

I’m using the required fish-control bookshelf to transfer only a control invariant, and the wake-visual skill because this policy must be grounded in both 3D moving-window views. Those instructions will determine the evidence checks and the format of the policy hypothesis.

The workspace does not have `rg`, so I’m falling back to `find`. I’ve confirmed the durable parent lesson already favors preserving the traveling bend while adding bounded body-frame steering; I’m now checking whether the sampled failures support that mechanism and which signals are actually available.

The visual comparison is decisive: the best sampled tail-only controller travels farther left and lowers distance by about 0.82L, but still accelerates upward into the same boundary; the parent’s equal head/tail bias produces an even broader U-turn and ends roughly 3.03L farther from the target. I’m consulting the bookshelf references now to choose a mechanism-level correction, not another scalar gain tweak.

The bookshelf’s half-cycle asymmetry primitive matches the evidence boundary: three static mean-curvature variants suppressed the carrier or retained the same exit, while posterior-only steering preserved propulsion. Before changing the policy, I’m recording a hypothesis that keeps the anterior oscillator untouched and moves steering into bounded, phase-aware posterior asymmetry with body-frame slip/rate feedback.

The candidate is now a single policy with reflection-odd feedback and no time, route, or coordinate memory. The bookshelf transfer specifically changed the actuator structure: steering modulates opposite posterior half-cycles while the anterior limit cycle stays centered. I’m now replacing the stale “test mean curvature” lesson with what the completed first-generation rollouts actually showed.

The required notes and durable lesson are both updated. Per the workspace contract, I’m invoking the dedicated non-CFD check runner now; it will verify the guidance delta, Julia policy contract, parameter schema, and editable-file boundary.

The configured check-runner model is unavailable in this account, so the invocation itself failed before executing commands. I’m running the exact three non-CFD commands from its immutable configuration locally and will repair any failure before finishing.

Two mandated checks pass: the evidence/guidance checker and the editable-boundary plus parameter-schema guard. The Julia executable is absent, so the runtime smoke check cannot run; I’m doing a final static schema/nonempty review and confirming no extra solver file was changed.

Produced exactly one candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1): bounded posterior half-cycle asymmetry driven by body-frame bearing, relative crossflow, and turn rate, while preserving the anterior oscillator.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): visual diagnosis, hypothesis, bookshelf transfer block, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:60): reusable negative lesson against anterior static-curvature recentering and evidence supporting posterior-only modulation.

Validation passed for guidance changes, file boundaries, parameter schema, and required nonempty files. The configured check-runner model and local Julia executable were unavailable, so the Julia runtime smoke check could not run. Formal CFD was not run.
